packs.name: Swiss Grid Report
packs.summary: Strict typographic grid, red accent, engineering-report clarity.
packs.directive: STYLE swiss-grid-report: white background, near-black text (#111111), one signal-red accent (#e63329) used only for section numbers and the single key figure per slide. Titles are sentence-case statements set large; body text small and dense but never below reading comfort. Everything aligns to an invisible 12-column grid — flush left, ragged right. Mathematics/formulas and tables are first-class content. Number every slide (small, top-right). No decorative elements whatsoever; hierarchy comes from size and position only.
packs.license: style adapted from open-design html-ppt 'swiss-grid' theme (MIT, @lewislulu)

packs.name: Terminal Green Tech
packs.summary: Dark terminal aesthetic for engineering and infra audiences.
packs.directive: STYLE terminal-green-tech: deep charcoal background (#0a0f0a), phosphor-green text (#33ff66), monospace-feel headings, amber (#ffb000) for warnings/caveats only. Titles read like shell prompts or release-note headlines ('deps: cut cold start by 60%'). Code snippets and command lines are hero content — render them as preformatted-style paragraphs. Data shown as tight tables. One idea per slide, terse phrasing, no marketing adjectives.
packs.license: style adapted from open-design html-ppt 'terminal-green' theme (MIT, @lewislulu)

packs.name: Warm Quarterly Magazine
packs.summary: Editorial quarter-in-review: warm paper, pull quotes, narrative flow.
packs.directive: STYLE warm-quarterly-magazine: warm paper (#f7f3ec), ink brown (#2b2320), muted gold accent (#b98a2f). Titles are editorial headlines — narrative, complete thoughts. Alternate rhythm: full-paragraph narrative slides punctuated by single big-number slides. Pull quotes (short, attributed) get their own slides. Sections open with a divider slide carrying only the section name and a one-line summary. Generous margins; nothing touches the edges.
packs.license: original kawai style vocabulary

packs.name: Dracula Night
packs.summary: Beloved dark palette: purple/pink/cyan on deep night blue.
packs.directive: STYLE dracula-night: background #282a36, text #f8f8f2, accents used sparingly and semantically — purple #bd93f9 for titles' key word, pink #ff79c6 for the hero number, cyan #8be9fd for code/technical terms, green #50fa7b only for positive deltas. Titles short and punchy. Code snippets welcome as first-class content. Playful but disciplined: max two accent colors per slide.
packs.license: style adapted from open-design html-ppt 'dracula' theme (MIT, @lewislulu)

packs.name: Tokyo Night
packs.summary: Muted neon on deep indigo — calm, modern, developer-chic.
packs.directive: STYLE tokyo-night: background #1a1b26, text #a9b1d6 with bright #c0caf5 for titles, accent #7aa2f7 (blue) as the workhorse, #9ece6a (green) for success metrics, #f7768e (red) sparingly for risks. Low-contrast backgrounds with high-contrast key content — the important element on each slide is the BRIGHTEST thing on it. Calm pacing: one idea, plenty of dark space.
packs.license: style adapted from open-design html-ppt 'tokyo-night' theme (MIT, @lewislulu)

packs.name: Nordic Cool
packs.summary: Muted arctic blues and greys — restrained, professional, frosty.
packs.directive: STYLE nordic-cool: background #2e3440 or light #eceff4, text #d8dee9 / #2e3440 respectively, accents from the frost scale (#8fbcbb, #88c0d0) with #bf616a reserved for the single most important number. No pure black or white — everything sits in the muted nord range. Titles understated; content speaks. Tables and timelines are preferred structures. The overall feel is calm competence.

packs.name: Gruvbox Warm
packs.summary: Retro warm earth tones — orange/yellow accents on aged paper or brown dark.
packs.directive: STYLE gruvbox-warm: background #fbf1c7 (light) or #282828 (dark), text #3c3836 / #ebdbb2, accents #d79921 (amber) and #fe8019 (orange) for emphasis, #98971a (olive) for positive metrics. Nostalgic, comfortable, slightly retro. Titles can carry personality ('The part everyone gets wrong'). Aliased, friendly tone; bullets short. Works especially well for postmortems and learnings decks.

packs.name: Solarized Paper
packs.summary: The classic low-fatigue palette on warm paper — long-meeting friendly.
packs.directive: STYLE solarized-paper: background #fdf6e3, text #657b83 with headings #073642, accent #268bd2 (blue) for key points, #b58900 (yellow) for numbers, #cb4b16 (orange) sparingly. Designed to be easy on eyes for long sessions. Titles are functional, not clever. Content density can run higher than most templates — this is a working deck, not a show deck. Tables, checklists, and step sequences are the natural slide shapes.
packs.license: style adapted from open-design html-ppt 'solarized-light' theme (MIT, @lewislulu)

packs.name: Neo-Brutalist
packs.summary: Loud blocks, thick borders, hard shadows — impossible to ignore.
packs.directive: STYLE neo-brutalist: background #fff or bold color fields (#ffd803 yellow, #a6fa86 green, #9dbdf2 blue) used as full-slide washes, thick black borders (#000, 3px) around key boxes, offset hard shadows. Text is heavy-weight and uppercase for titles ('THIS CHANGES EVERYTHING'), normal case for body. One shouting element per slide — a giant number, one word, one claim. Rotate background color per section. Chaos is choreographed: loud, but aligned.
packs.license: style adapted from open-design html-ppt 'neo-brutalism' theme (MIT, @lewislulu)

packs.name: Bauhaus Blocks
packs.summary: Primary-color geometry: circles, bars, and grids that structure the argument.
packs.directive: STYLE bauhaus-blocks: background #f4f1ea, primary red #d02e26, blue #1c4c9c, yellow #f2b705, black for text. Every slide composes from simple geometric vocabulary — a full-width color bar as a section marker, a circle holding the hero number, rectangles as content zones. Titles set bold and low on the slide. Form follows the argument: comparison slides split the canvas in half; sequences use left-to-right blocks. No ornament — geometry IS the decoration.
packs.license: style adapted from open-design html-ppt 'bauhaus' theme (MIT, @lewislulu)

packs.name: Japanese Minimal
packs.summary: Ma (negative space), one image or phrase per slide, profound restraint.
packs.directive: STYLE japanese-minimal: background #ffffff or #f6f4f0, text #333 with warm grey #888 for secondary, a single vermilion #e34234 seal-like accent appearing on at most a third of slides. Enormous negative space — content occupies at most a third of the slide. Each slide holds ONE phrase, ONE number, or ONE image with a one-line caption. Titles may be a single word. Silence is the design: what you leave off the slide says as much as what's on it.
packs.license: style adapted from open-design html-ppt 'japanese-minimal' theme (MIT, @lewislulu)

packs.name: Cyberpunk Neon
packs.summary: High-voltage magenta/cyan on black — product launches and bold visions.
packs.directive: STYLE cyberpunk-neon: background #050505 with subtle grid or scanline feel implied via content placement, text #e8e8e8, neon magenta #ff2a6d and cyan #05d9e8 as dueling accents, #d1f7ff for glows described in text emphasis. Titles are declarations of the future ('Shipping the impossible'), set bold. Use contrast extremes: tiny dense captions against one enormous glowing claim. For vision/launch decks only — never for financial reporting.
packs.license: style adapted from open-design html-ppt 'cyberpunk-neon' theme (MIT, @lewislulu)

packs.name: Memphis Pop
packs.summary: Playful 80s post-modern: squiggles, confetti geometry, joyful color clashes.
packs.directive: STYLE memphis-pop: background #fff or pastel (#ffeee0, #e0f7fa), text #212121, clashing accents used confidently: #ff5a5f coral, #00c2b8 teal, #ffce00 yellow, #7c4dff violet. Titles are fun, conversational, exclamation-friendly. Decorative vocabulary: scattered small shapes (triangle, circle, zigzag) described as bordered inline elements at slide corners — never overlapping content. Energy high, hierarchy still strict: one message per slide, confetti stays in the margins.

packs.name: Midcentury Modern
packs.summary: 1950s optimism: mustard, teal, walnut — warm geometry and confident serif feel.
packs.directive: STYLE midcentury-modern: background #f2e8d5, text #3f3a30, palette mustard #e3b23c, teal #2a9d8f, terracotta #c96f4a, deep walnut #6b4f3a for weight. Titles confident and succinct with a wry warmth ('The good old days are now'). Content zones feel like furniture: rounded rectangles, balanced asymmetry, one anchor visual per slide. Works for brand, culture, and annual-review decks.

packs.name: Academic Paper
packs.summary: Serious, citation-friendly, conference-ready restraint.
packs.directive: STYLE academic-paper: white background, near-black serif-feel text (#1a1a1a), institutional deep blue (#003366) for headings, no other accent colors except a single highlight (#c8102e) for the core finding. Titles state findings precisely ('Sample bias explains 70% of the variance'). Structure follows paper conventions: Motivation, Method, Results, Limitations, Conclusion. Evidence density is high — every claim carries its source inline. No hype words; hedging is a feature.
packs.license: style adapted from open-design html-ppt 'academic-paper' theme (MIT, @lewislulu)

packs.name: Magazine Bold
packs.summary: Full-bleed color, giant display type, editorial confidence.
packs.directive: STYLE magazine-bold: each section opens with a full-wash background in a saturated editorial color (crimson #c0392b, cobalt #22499c, forest #14532d — rotate), text white or cream. Display titles are HUGE — 6 words maximum, set like a magazine cover line. Body copy runs in short confident paragraphs. Pull numbers out at poster scale. The deck should feel like flipping through a bold print feature: rhythm between loud section openers and quieter content spreads.
